mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle, leading to compressed discount rates on equity cash flows and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during easing periods, or FEDFUNDS does not decline consistently over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days due to heightened economic uncertainty and reduced consumer confidence.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negative when UNRATE crosses above 4.5%, or the effect persists beyond the 20-day window.

mechanism_narrative: When both federal funds rates remain below 4% and quarterly GDP growth exceeds 16,000 billion chained 2017 dollars, the combined easing and strong demand drive positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not positive when both FEDFUNDS <4% and GDPC1 >16,000, or the effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: In high supply environments (INDPRO >105), a decline in federal funds rates below 4% creates a synergistic effect, boosting S&P 500 returns over 20 days as monetary easing complements robust supply-side growth.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not positive when FEDFUNDS <4% and INDPRO >105, or the effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% signals labor market strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns within the next 5 trading days as investor confidence surges.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not positive when UNRATE drops below 4.0%, or the decline does not persist beyond the 5-day window.

mechanism_narrative: When quarterly GDP growth surpasses 17,000 billion chained 2017 dollars within a month, investors anticipate robust economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 returns within 5 days as market anticipates sustained expansion.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 exceeds 17,000 in the next month
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not positive when GDPC1 crosses above 17,000, or the effect fades before the 5-day window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong demand (GDPC1 >17,000) combined with falling unemployment (UNRATE <4.0%) creates a dual positive signal, amplifying S&P 500 returns over 60 days as market optimizes for sustained growth and labor market stability.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not positive when both GDPC1 >17,000 and UNRATE <4.0%, or the effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: In high supply environments (INDPRO >105), a decline in federal funds rates below 4% predicts positive S&P 500 returns within 5 days as monetary easing enhances equity valuations amid robust production.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not positive when FEDFUNDS <4% in high supply periods, or the effect does not materialize within the 5-day window.
